ex.en: You have to share the cake equally.
ex.ja: 君たちはケーキを平等に分けなければならない。

en: The condition of being fit, suitable or appropriate.
The cultivation of an attractive and/or healthy physique.

fitness.ety: From fit + -ness. First attested in the 16th century, with the physical sense from 1935.

ex.en: The physical fitness courses are required for everyone.
ex.ja: 体育の授業は全員が必修です。

ex.en: No one doubts her fitness for the post.
ex.ja: 彼女がその地位にふさわしいということは、だれも疑っていない。

ex.en: She exercises every day at a fitness club.
ex.ja: 彼女はフィットネスクラブで毎日訓練する。

en: The condition of being friends.
A friendly relationship, or a relationship as friends.

From Middle English frendschipe, frendshipe, from Old English frēondsċiepe, from Proto-West Germanic *friundskapi. Equivalent to friend + -ship.

ex.en: A true friendship is more valuable than money.
ex.ja: 真の友情はお金より尊い。

ex.en: I am bound to him by a close friendship.
ex.ja: 私は固い友情で彼と結ばれている。

ex.en: If you do that, our friendship will be over.
ex.ja: そんなことするんなら、絶交だ。

Doublet of idiota. By surface analysis, idi- + -ot.

ex.en: Where does that idiot think he is going?
ex.ja: あの馬鹿、どこへ行くつもりだ？

ex.en: Why do you love an idiot like me?
ex.ja: こんなばかな私をどうして愛してくれるの？

ex.en: I was an idiot to believe Tom.
ex.ja: トムを信じた私がバカだったよ。

en: Of a characteristic: extreme or very high or strong in degree; severe; also, excessive, towering.
Of a thing: possessing some characteristic to an extreme or very high or strong degree.

intense.ety: From Late Middle English intens, intense (“ardent, fervent; extreme, great, intense”), borrowed from Old French intense (modern French intense), or directly from its etymon Latin intēnsus (“strained, stretched tight; intense; attentive; violent; (rare) eager, intent”), the perfect passive participle of intendō (“to stretch out, strain”), from in- (prefix meaning ‘in, inside, within’) + tendō (“to extend, stretch”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tend- (“to extend, stretch”)).

ex.en: How are you keeping off this intense heat?
ex.ja: 猛暑をどうしのいでいますか。

ex.en: There was an intense pain in my head.
ex.ja: 頭に激しい痛みがあった。

ex.en: This intense heat doesn't seem to bother you.
ex.ja: こんなに暑いのに君は平気みたいだね。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ tens（伸ばす）+ e。ぴんと張りつめた →「激しい・強烈な」。

en: The duration of the life of someone or something.
A long period of time.

lifetime.ety: From Middle English lyftyme, equivalent to life + time. Cognate with Icelandic líftími (“lifetime”). Compare also Saterland Frisian Lieuwendstied, Dutch leeftijd and levenstijd, German Low German Levenstied, German Lebenszeit, Danish livstid, Swedish livstid.

ex.en: Her dream of a lifetime finally came true.
ex.ja: 彼女の一生の夢がついに叶った。

ex.en: This is the chance of a lifetime.
ex.ja: これは私の生涯にとって千載一遇の機会だ。

ex.en: He made a great fortune in his lifetime.
ex.ja: 彼は一代で巨万の富を得た。

Any of a class of consonant sounds that includes l and r.
Flowing freely like water; fluid; not solid and not gaseous; composed of particles that move freely among each other on the slightest pre…
Easily sold or disposed of without losing value.

From Middle English liquide, from Old French liquide, from Latin liquidus (“fluid, liquid, moist”), from liqueō (“to be liquid, be fluid”). Doublet of liquidus. As a term for a consonant, it comes from Latin liquida (cōnsōnāns), a calque of Ancient Greek

ex.en: You should not drink a lot of liquid.
ex.ja: 水分を控えてください。

ex.en: The liquid gave off a strong smell.
ex.ja: その液体は強烈な匂いを発した。

ex.en: Matter can exist as a solid, liquid, or gas.
ex.ja: 物体は固体、液体、気体として存在する。

en: An item's composition.
Cosmetics; colorants and other substances applied to the skin to alter its appearance.

makeup.ety: Deverbal from make up. Noun sense 2 is a semantic loan from French maquillage, from maquiller (“to make up, fabricate”).

ex.en: My mother put on makeup before going out.
ex.ja: 母は出かける前に化粧をした。

ex.en: I don't like heavy makeup on a young girl.
ex.ja: 私は若い娘の厚化粧は好まない。

ex.en: The princess was wearing too much makeup.
ex.ja: 王女があくどい化粧をしていた。

en: A stamped metal disc used as a personal ornament, a charm, or a religious object.
A stamped or cast metal object (usually a disc), particularly one awarded as a prize or reward.
To win a medal.
To award a medal to.

medal.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Middle French medaille, medale, from Italian medaglia (originally "half a denarius"), from Early Medieval Latin medālia, feminine derived via dissimilation (/dj–lj/ > /d–lj/) from mediālia, neuter plural of Late Latin mediālis (“middle”, adjective), from Classical Latin medius.

ex.en: He's been awarded a gold medal once.
ex.ja: 彼はいちど金メダルをもらったことがある。

ex.en: They awarded him a gold medal for his achievement.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼の業績に対して金メダルを授与した。

ex.en: I won my first gold medal.
ex.ja: 初めて金メダルを手にしました。

en: A legal agreement in which a borrower pledges real property as collateral for a loan used to purchase or refinance that property.
To borrow against a property, to obtain a loan for another purpose by giving away the right of seizure to the lender over a fixed propert…
To pledge and make liable; to make subject to obligation; to achieve an immediate result by paying for it in the long term.

mortgage.ety: From Middle English morgage and Middle French mortgage, from Anglo-Norman morgage, from Old French mort gage (“dead pledge”), after a translation of judicial Medieval Latin mortuum wadium, with wadium from Frankish *wadi (“wager, pledge”). Compare gage and also wage. So called because rents and profits from the land were owed to the lender for as long as the gage existed (comparable to interest on a loan today), as opposed to the living gage, in which rents and profits automatically reduced the debt (paying it off over time).

ex.en: The bank holds a mortgage on his building.
ex.ja: 銀行は彼のビルを抵当に取っている。

ex.en: My house is a mortgage-free house.
ex.ja: 私の家はローンの支払いが終わいる。

ex.en: I suffered from my mortgage loan.
ex.ja: 私は住宅ローンで苦しんだ。

en: Telling a story.
Overly talkative; garrulous.
The systematic recitation of an event or series of events.
That which is narrated.

narrative.ety: Borrowed from Middle Scots narrative, nerrative, from Middle French narratif, from Latin narrātīvus, from narrō (“to narrate”). By surface analysis, Latin narr- + -ate + -ive.

ex.en: She gave a narrative of her strange experience.
ex.ja: 彼女は自分の奇妙な経験を語った。

ex.en: That is not what the narrative is about.
ex.ja: それはその物語の述べるところではない。

ex.en: The mystery contains more dialogue than narrative.
ex.ja: その推理小説は地の文よりも会話の部分の方が多い。

en: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.
Of little extent; very limited; circumscribed.
A narrow passage, especially a contracted part of a stream, lake, or sea; a strait connecting two bodies of water.
To reduce in width or extent; to contract.
To get narrower.

narrow.ety:
From Middle English narow, narowe, narewe, narwe, naru, from Old English nearu (“narrow, strait, confined, constricted, not spacious, limited, petty; limited, poor, restricted; oppressive, causing anxiety (of that which restricts free action of body or mind), causing or accompanied by difficulty, hardship, oppressive; oppressed, not having free action; strict, severe”), from Proto-West Germanic *naru, from Proto-Germanic *narwaz (“constricted, narrow”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ner- (“to turn, bend, twist, constrict”).
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian naar, noar, noor, nåår (“narrow”),

ex.en: This house is too narrow to live in.
ex.ja: この家は住むには狭すぎる。

ex.en: The gate is too narrow for a car.
ex.ja: その門は狭すぎて車は入れません。

ex.en: The gate was too narrow for the truck.
ex.ja: 門はトラックには狭過ぎた。

en: To notice or view, especially carefully or with attention to detail.
To follow or obey the custom, practice, or rules (especially of a religion).

observe.ety: From Middle French observer, from Old French observer, from Latin observō (“to watch”), from ob- (“before”) + servō (“to keep”), from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to guard”). Cognate with Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐍂𐍅𐌰 (sarwa, “weapons, armour”), Old English searu (“device”).

ex.en: The boy observed the growth of the plant.
ex.ja: その少年は植物の成長を観察した。

ex.en: I observed that it had already got dark.
ex.ja: あたりがもう暗くなっていることに気がついた。

ex.en: The police observed the man enter the bank.
ex.ja: 警察はその男が銀行に入るのを見つけた。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ serv（保つ・見守る）。注意深く見守る →「観察する・（規則を）守る・述べる」。

en: On occasion: at relatively infrequent intervals, from time to time, sometimes.

occasionally.ety: From Middle English occasionally, occasionaly, occasyoneely, occasyonly, equivalent to occasional + -ly.

ex.en: The speaker occasionally referred to his notes.
ex.ja: 講演者は時折メモを参照した。

ex.en: Let's occasionally change where we go to eat out.
ex.ja: いつもと変えてたまに外で食事しよう。

ex.en: I occasionally meet him at the club.
ex.ja: 時折クラブで彼に会います。

en: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
The contents of such a receptacle.
To wash in a pan (of earth, sand etc. when searching for gold).
To disparage; to belittle; to put down; to harshly criticize, especially a work (book, movie, etc.)
Pansexual or panromantic.

ex.ja: 鍋に油入れた？

ex.ja: その鍋に触らないで。すごく熱いから。

ex.en: The handle of this pan is easy to hold.
ex.ja: このフライパンのとっては持ちやすい。

en: The branch of science concerned with the study of the properties and interactions of space, time, matter and energy.
The physical aspects of a phenomenon or a system, especially those examined or studied scientifically.

physics.ety: 1580s; from physic (see also -ics), from Middle English phisik, from Old French fisike (“natural science, art of healing”), from Latin physica (“study of nature”), from Ancient Greek φυσική (phusikḗ), feminine singular of φυσικός (phusikós, “natural; physical”), from Ancient Greek φύσις (phúsis, “origin; nature, property”), from Ancient Greek φύω (phúō, “produce; bear; grow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

ex.en: I have to bone up on my physics.
ex.ja: 私は一生懸命物理に取り組まなければならない。

ex.ja: 英語の好きな生徒もいるし、物理の好きな生徒もいる。

ex.en: Which do you like better, physics or chemistry?
ex.ja: 物理学と化学だとどちらが好きですか？

en: The act, process, or result of reducing.
The amount or rate by which something is reduced, e.g. in price.

reduction.ety: From Middle English reduccion, a borrowing from Old French reducion, from Latin reductiō, reductiōnem. Equivalent to reduce + -tion.

ex.en: A further reduction would make us go into the red.
ex.ja: これ以上の値引きは、私どもを赤字に追いやるでしょう。

ex.en: We cannot offer a further price reduction under the current circumstances.
ex.ja: 現状では、これ以上の値引きはいたしかねます。

ex.en: We would ask you to give us a price reduction of 5%.
ex.ja: それを５％値引きしていただけますか。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ duct（導く）+ ion。元へ引き戻すこと →「削減・縮小」。reduce（減らす）。

en: To bend back (light, etc.) from a surface.
To be bent back (light, etc.) from a surface.

reflect.ety: From Old French reflecter (“to bend back, turn back”), from Latin reflectō (“to reflect”), from re- (“again”) + flectō (“to bend, to curve”). Compare English reflex.

ex.en: It is time to reflect on your past.
ex.ja: 自分の過去をじっくり振り返ってみてもよいころだ。

ex.en: This decision will reflect on his future career.
ex.ja: この決定は彼の将来に悪影響をもたらすだろう。

ex.en: His speech didn't reflect the sense of the party.
ex.ja: 彼の演説は党の意向を反映したものではなかった。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ flect（曲げる）。光を後ろへ曲げ返す →「反射する・反映する・よく考える」。

en: Received (used in radio communications to acknowledge that a message has been received and understood)
To acknowledge by saying "roger".

roger.ety: From Roger, used circa 1940 in UK and US military communication to represent "R" when spelling out a word. "R" is the first letter in received, used to acknowledge understanding a message. "Roger" for "received" was in spoken usage in air traffic radio parlance by 1950.

ex.en: Roger works from morning till night.
ex.ja: ロジャーは朝から晩まで働いている。

ex.en: Hi, Roger. I'm pretty good!
ex.ja: こんにちは、ロジャー。とっても元気よ。

ex.en: Roger is a party animal.
ex.ja: ロジャーはパーティーが大好きだ。

en: The calcareous or chitinous external covering of mollusks, crustaceans, and some other invertebrates.
Any mollusk having such a covering.
To remove the outer covering or shell of something.
To bombard, to fire projectiles at, especially with artillery.

Cognates
Cognate with Dutch schil (“bark, rind, skin; crust; shell; slice”), Danish skæl (“scale; dandruff”), Faroese and Icelandic skel (“shell”), Norwegian Bokmål

ex.en: I came out of my shell in college.
ex.ja: 大学生の時に心を開きました。

ex.en: The shell of an egg is easily broken.
ex.ja: 卵の殻は壊れやすい。

ex.en: I watched Ghost in the Shell today.
ex.ja: 今日「ゴースト・イン・ザ・シェル」を観たよ。

en: Laughable or amusing through foolishness or a foolish appearance.
Absurdly large.
Sillily: in a silly manner.
A silly person.
A term of address.

silly.ety:
From Middle English seely, sēlī, from Old English sǣliġ, ġesǣliġ (“lucky, fortunate”), from Proto-West Germanic *sālīg, from *sāli; equivalent to seel (“happiness, bliss”) + -y. Doublet of Seelie.
The semantic evolution is “lucky” to “innocent” to “naive” to “foolish”. Compare the similar evolution of daft (originally meaning “accommodating”), and almost the reverse with nice (originally meaning “ignorant”).

ex.en: Don't put such silly thoughts into his head.
ex.ja: 彼にそんなばかげた考えをたたきこむな。

ex.en: It was silly of you to trust them.
ex.ja: 君がやつらを信じたのはばかだった。

ex.en: How can you say such a silly thing?
ex.ja: どうしてそんな馬鹿な事が言えるんですか。

en: The conversion of text from one language to another.
The discipline or study of translating written language (as opposed to interpretation, which concerns itself with spoken language).

translation.ety: From Middle English translacioun (“transfer, translation”), from Anglo-Norman translacioun, from Latin trānslātiō, from trānslāt-, the supine stem of trānsferō (“to transfer, transport, transform, translate”). Equivalent to translate + -ion. Displaced native Old English wending.

ex.en: The translation is quite true to the original.
ex.ja: その翻訳は原文に極めて忠実である。

ex.en: I am grateful for the question and translation.
ex.ja: 質問と訳をありがとう。

ex.en: This sentence isn't a translation. It's the original.
ex.ja: この文は訳ではありません。これが原文です。

en: Able to be seen.

visible.ety: From Middle English visible, from Old French visible, from Late Latin visibilis (“that may be seen”), from Latin videre (“to see”), past participle visus; see vision. Displaced native Old English ġesewenlīċ.

ex.en: It isn't really visible to the naked eye.
ex.ja: それは裸眼にはそこまではっきり見ることはできない。

ex.en: It's not really visible to the naked eye.
ex.ja: それは裸眼にはそこまではっきり見ることはできない。

ex.en: The number of visible stars is very great.
ex.ja: 目に見える星の数は無数です。

note.ja: vis（見る）+ ible（〜できる）。見ることができる →「目に見える」。invisible（見えない）。

en: Yes.
Yes.

yep.ety: Representing yeah pronounced with the mouth snapped closed at the end (yeah + -p). Compare yup and nope. Compare also German jap (“yep”).

en: An alteration or change for the better; correction of a fault or of faults; reformation of life by quitting vices.
In public bodies, any alteration made or proposed to be made in a bill or motion that adds, changes, substitutes, or omits.

amendment.ety: From French amendement, from Late Latin amendamentum, equivalent to amend + -ment.

en: A figure formed by two rays which start from a common point (a plane angle) or by three planes that intersect (a solid angle).
The measure of such a figure. In the case of a plane angle, this is the ratio (or proportional to the ratio) of the arc length to the rad…
To place (something) at an angle.
To change direction rapidly.

ex.en: Let's approach this problem from a different angle.
ex.ja: この問題を別の面から取り組んでみよう。

ex.en: We will consider the problem from a different angle.
ex.ja: 別の角度から問題を検討する。

ex.en: An angle of 90 degrees is called a right angle.
ex.ja: ９０度の角度は直角と呼ばれている。

To be accepted in a group.
Of, belonging to.

ex.en: I feel that I don't really belong here.
ex.ja: どうもここは私には場違いな気がする。

ex.en: You never put things back where they belong.
ex.ja: 君は相変わらず物を元の場所に戻さないね。

ex.en: You belong in a better place than this.
ex.ja: 君はもっとましな地位にあるべき人だ。

en: An overseer of congregations: either any such overseer, generally speaking, or (in Eastern Orthodoxy, Catholicism, Anglicanism, etc.) an …
A chief of the Festival of Fools or St. Nicholas Day.
To act as a bishop, to perform the duties of a bishop, especially to confirm another's membership in the church.
To make a bishop.

bishop.ety:

Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also Middle English bisp (“bishop”).
* The Tyndale Bible uses native English overseer instead.

ex.en: The bishops were in favor of the proposition.
ex.ja: 司教達はその提案に賛成であった。

ex.ja: 司教は、自暴自棄になった移民たちを哀れんで助けを与えた。

en: As a rule; frequently; usually.

commonly.ety: Inherited from Middle English comunly; equivalent to common + -ly.

ex.en: Women commonly live longer than men.
ex.ja: 女性は通常男性よりも長生きする。

ex.en: This sentence is commonly used.
ex.ja: この文はよく使われるよ。

ex.en: Antibiotics are commonly enzymatic inhibitors.
ex.ja: 抗生物質は一般的に酵素の阻害剤である。

en: Intended for defence; protective.
Intended to deter attack.
A means, attitude or position of defense. Chiefly in on the defensive.

defensive.ety: From Middle French défensif. Morphologically defense + -ive.

ex.en: Defensive driving can help you avoid accidents.
ex.ja: 予防運転は事故を防ぎます。

en: The extent to which a resource is used for the intended purpose.
The ratio of useful work to energy expended. Often given the symbol η.

efficiency.ety: From Latin efficientia, equivalent to efficient + -cy.

ex.en: He put forward a plan for improving office efficiency.
ex.ja: 彼は事務効率をよくする案を出した。

ex.en: Efficiency is the dominant idea in business.
ex.ja: 商売では能率のよさということが最も重要な考えである。

ex.en: That makes for efficiency.
ex.ja: そうすれば能率が上がりますよ。

en: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
An undertaking, venture, or project, especially a daring and courageous one.
To undertake an enterprise, or something hazardous or difficult.
To undertake; to begin and attempt to perform; to venture upon.

enterprise.ety: From Old French via Middle English and Middle French entreprise, feminine past participle of entreprendre (“to undertake”), from entre (“in between”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin inter + prehendō, see prehensile.

ex.en: He played an important part in the enterprise.
ex.ja: 彼はその事業において重要な役割を演じた。

ex.en: Building the steel factory was a great enterprise.
ex.ja: その製鉄工場を建てるのは非常に大変な事業だった。

ex.en: Commercial Code can be called an enterprise method.
ex.ja: 商法は企業法といえる。

note.ja: enter（= inter 間に）+ pris（取る）+ e。手中に取ること →（困難なことに着手する）→「企業・事業・冒険心」。

en: A test under controlled conditions made to either demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the effic…
To conduct an experiment.
To try something to observe the results.

experiment.ety: From Middle English experiment, from Old French esperiment (French expérience), from Latin experimentum (“experience, attempt, experiment”), from experior (“to experience, to attempt”), itself from ex + *perior, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *per-.

ex.en: We used the following procedures in this experiment.
ex.ja: この実験には以下の手段を使用した。

ex.en: They carried out a new experiment in chemistry.
ex.ja: 彼らは化学の新しい実験をした。

ex.en: We were disappointed with the results of the experiment.
ex.ja: 私達は実験の結果にがっかりした。

en: A place for discussion.
A gathering for the purpose of discussion; a symposium.

forum.ety: From Latin forum (“public market place, forum”). Doublet of fuero and door.

ex.en: I moved the forum to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: The forum was moved to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: I do not have an account in these forums.
ex.ja: これらのフォームのアカウントを私はもってません。

en: Any plant of the family Poaceae, characterized by leaves that arise from nodes in the stem and leaf bases that wrap around the stem, espe…
Any of the various plants that are not in the family Poaceae that resemble grasses.
To lay out on the grass; to knock down (an opponent etc.).
To cover with grass or with turf.

ex.en: This grass is too wet to sit on.
ex.ja: この芝生は座れないほどぬれている。

en: In the future from now.
As a result; therefore, for this reason.

hence.ety:
A later Middle English spelling, retaining the voiceless -s, of hennes (henne + adverbial genitive ending -s), from Old English heonan (“away", "hence”), from a Proto-West Germanic *hin-, from Proto-Germanic *hiz, and Proto-Germanic *-anē.
Cognate with Old Saxon hinan, Old High German hinnan (German hinnen), Dutch heen, Swedish hän. Related to Old English her (“here”).

ex.en: Hence, I shall have to stay here.
ex.ja: それゆえここにとどまらざるを得ないだろう。

ex.en: What will become of the world thirty years hence?
ex.ja: 今から３０年後に世界はどうなるだろう？

ex.en: It will be all the same a hundred years hence.
ex.ja: 百年後にはみな同じになる。

en: Increasing in amount or intensity.

increasingly.ety: From Middle English encreessingli, equivalent to increasing + -ly.

ex.en: Modern finance is becoming increasingly complicated and sophisticated.
ex.ja: 現代の金融は一段と複雑かつ高度になってきている。

ex.en: In recent years electronic computers have become increasingly important.
ex.ja: 近年では、電子コンピューターがますます重要になってきた。

ex.en: The world's aviation industry is growing increasingly worried about crashes.
ex.ja: 世界の航空産業は墜落事故についての懸念を募らせている。

en: Any of the numerous species of birds belonging to several genera within the family Corvidae, including Garrulus, Cyanocitta, Aphelocoma, …
Any of various other birds of similar appearance and behaviour.

jay.ety: From Middle English jay, from Old French jai ("jay"; Modern French geai), either from Late Latin gaius (“jay”), or from Old French gai (“gay, merry”), so named due to its plumage, from Old Frankish *gāhi (“quick, impetuous”), from Proto-Germanic *ganhuz, *ganhwaz (“sudden”), cognate with Dutch gaai (“jay”). More at gay.

ex.en: Jay picked up the old scissors.
ex.ja: ジェイはその古いはさみを拾い上げた。

zh: 新聞工作者 /新闻工作者

One whose occupation is journalism, originally only writing in the printed press.

ex.ja: この橋の上流に水車小屋がある。

ex.ja: 水車小屋は皆自分の水車に水を引く。

en: A favorable opportunity; a convenient or timely chance.
The time when something happens.
To cause; to produce; to induce

occasion.ety: From Middle English occasioun, from Middle French occasion, from Old French occasiun, from Latin occāsiōnem, noun of action from perfect passive participle occāsus, from verb occidō, from prefix ob- (“down", "away”) + verb cadō (“fall”).

ex.en: He offered his congratulations on the happy occasion.
ex.ja: そのめでたいときに当たり彼は祝辞を述べた。

ex.en: We meet him on occasion at the club.
ex.ja: 私たちは時折クラブで彼に出会います。

ex.en: I meet her on occasion at the club.
ex.ja: 私は彼女にときおりクラブで会います。

note.ja: oc（〜に向かって）+ cas（落ちる）+ ion。降りかかってくる時 →「場合・機会・行事」。

en: A step taken with the foot.
The distance covered in a step (or sometimes two), either vaguely or according to various specific set measurements.
Describing a bowler who bowls fast balls.
To walk back and forth in a small distance.
To walk along or through sth with regular strides.
With all due respect to.

pace.ety: From Middle English pase, from Anglo-Norman pas, Old French pas, and their source, Latin passus. Doublet of pas and fathom; compare also pass. Cognate with pass, Spanish pasear, paso.

ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

ex.en: I want to work at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースで仕事したい。

ex.en: I want to go at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

en: One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
Somebody in a team who does not do their fair share of the work.
To ride as a passenger in a vehicle.

passenger.ety: From Old French passagier with intrusive n (see etymology of messenger).

ex.en: Why didn't they draw up a passenger list?
ex.ja: 彼らはなぜ乗客名簿を作らなかったのだろう。

ex.en: The bag I left on the passenger seat is missing!
ex.ja: 助手席に置いていた鞄がない！

ex.en: All the passengers were killed in the crash.
ex.ja: その墜落事故で乗客は全員死亡した。

en: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
The bullpen.
To enclose in a pen.

pen.ety:
From Middle English pen, penne (“enclosure for animals”), from Old English penn (“enclosure, fold, pen”), from Proto-Germanic *pennō, *pannijō (“pin, bolt, nail, tack”), from Proto-Indo-European *bend- (“pointed peg, nail, edge”). Related to pin.
Sense “prison” originally figurative extension to “enclosure for persons” (1845), later influenced by penitentiary (“prison”), being analyzed as an abbreviation (1884).

ex.en: Please pick up the pen from the floor.
ex.ja: 床からペンを拾って下さい。

ex.en: To tell the truth, I've lost your pen.
ex.ja: 実を言うと、あなたのペンをなくしてしまったのです。

ex.en: Which is longer, this pen or that one?
ex.ja: このペンとあのペンではどちらが長いですか。

en: An honorary title of the Roman Catholic bishop of Rome as father and head of his church, a sovereign of the Vatican city state.
Any similarly absolute and 'infallible' authority.
To act as or like a pope.
To convert to Roman Catholicism.

pope.ety: From Middle English pope, popa, from Old English pāpa, from Vulgar Latin papa (title for priests and bishops, esp. and by 8th c. only the bishop of Rome), from early Medieval Greek παπᾶς (papâs, title for priests and bishops, especially by 3rd c. the bishop of Alexandria), from late Ancient Greek πάπας (pápas, title for priests and bishops, in the sense of spiritual father), from πάππας (páppas, “papa, daddy”).

ex.en: We have a Pope.
ex.ja: われらは教皇を得た。

ex.en: The pope appeared in his red robe.
ex.ja: 法王は赤い法衣をまとって現れた。

en: A control or occupancy of something for which one does not necessarily have private property rights.
Something that is owned.

possession.ety: From Latin possessiō, possessiōnis. Equivalent to possess + -ion.

ex.en: I have never had more than $500 in my possession.
ex.ja: 私は５００ドル以上を持ち歩いたことがありません。

ex.en: He is in possession of this land.
ex.ja: 彼はこの土地を所有している。

ex.en: All his possessions are contained in that box.
ex.ja: 彼の所持品は全部あの箱に入っている。

Steep, changing altitude quickly. (of a slope)
A rough section of a river or stream which is difficult to navigate due to the swift and turbulent motion of the water.

ex.ja: その都市の急速な発展に私たちは驚いた。

ex.ja: 世界の人口は急激に増加している。

en: The ordinal form of the number six.
The person or thing in the sixth position.
One of six equal parts of a whole.

sixth.ety: From earlier sixt, from Middle English sixte, from Old English siexta, from Proto-Germanic *sehstô. By surface analysis, six + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: June is the sixth month of the year.
ex.ja: 「６月」は１年の中で６回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: She knew it by a sixth sense.
ex.ja: 彼女は第六感でそれが分かった。

ex.en: The office has been transferred up to the sixth floor.
ex.ja: 事務所は６階に移った。

en: To rotate, revolve, gyrate (usually quickly); to partially or completely rotate to face another direction.
To enter, or remain in, a spin (abnormal stalled flight mode).
Circular motion, usually rapid.
A state of confusion or disorientation.

spin.ety:
From Middle English spinnen, from Old English spinnan, from Proto-Germanic *spinnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁-.

Cognate with Dutch, German spinnen (“to spin”), Luxembourgish spannen (“to spin”), Yiddish שפּינען (shpinen, “spin”), Danish spinde (“to spin”), Faroese, Icelandic and Swedish spinna (“to spin”), Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk spinne (“to spin”), Gothic 𐍃𐍀𐌹𐌽𐌽𐌰𐌽 (spinnan, “to spin”).

ex.ja: 目が回るほど忙しいよ。

ex.en: After dinner, we took a spin around town in my car.
ex.ja: 食後、私の車で町を一走りした。

ex.ja: 暑さで頭が回らない。

A commercial lasting 30 seconds.

Acceptable, proper or correct; in accordance with the rules.

ex.ja: その切符は一週間有効です。

ex.ja: この列車乗車券は３カ月有効だ。

en: Relating to or characteristic of life.
Necessary to the continuation of life; being the seat of life; being that on which life depends.

ex.en: Public opinion plays a vital role in politics.
ex.ja: 世論は政治の領域で重要な役割を演ずる。

ex.ja: 水は極めて重要な天然資源の１つだ。

ex.ja: 実際、睡眠は人間にはどうしても欠かせない。

funeral.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French funerailles pl (“funeral rites”), from Medieval Latin fūnerālia (“funeral rites”), originally neuter plural of Late Latin fūnerālis (“having to do with a funeral”), from Latin fūnus (“funeral, death, corpse”), origin unknown, perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰew- (“to die”). Singular and plural used interchangeably in English until circa 1700. The adjective funereal is first attested 1725, by influence of Middle French funerail, from Latin funereus, from funus. First attested in 1437.
Displaced native Old English līcþeġnung (literally “dead body service
